subsystems.name: Survey imaging and remote sensing
subsystems.role: looks at surfaces and orbits at the resolution needed to spot something that should not be there.
parts: orbital cameras reaching roughly half a metre per pixel at the Moon
synthetic-aperture radar for shallow subsurface structure
wide-field ground telescopes that sweep the sky for small bodies

subsystems.name: Natural-process baselines
subsystems.role: the reference library that decides whether a candidate is genuinely anomalous.
parts: catalogue of human mission hardware and orbital debris

subsystems.name: Anomaly triage pipeline
subsystems.role: turns millions of images into a short list worth a second look.
parts: machine-learning classifiers trained on known geology

subsystems.name: Characterisation instruments
subsystems.role: measures composition, shape and internal structure of candidates.

subsystems.name: Physical sample recovery
subsystems.role: the only way to settle a claim is to hold the material.
parts: ocean-floor magnetic sled and sieve for meteor debris
fireball trajectory data to locate a fall site

subsystems.name: Data infrastructure and coordination
subsystems.role: makes results checkable rather than anecdotal.

buildSteps.title: Define the target signature
buildSteps.detail: Agree in advance on what counts as unexplained: shapes, alloys, isotopic ratios or thermal behaviour that known geology, weathering and human hardware cannot produce.

buildSteps.title: Build the baseline catalogue
buildSteps.detail: Compile every natural terrain type and every piece of human hardware in the Solar System so candidates can be tested against them.

buildSteps.title: Choose search volumes
buildSteps.detail: Prioritise places where evidence survives: the lunar surface, Earth co-orbital asteroids, the Sun–Earth Lagrange points, and stable high orbits.

buildSteps.title: Mine existing archives
buildSteps.detail: Reprocess decades of lunar and asteroid imagery with modern detection software — much of the data already exists and has never been examined for this purpose.

buildSteps.title: Run dedicated imaging campaigns
buildSteps.detail: Task orbiters and survey telescopes to re-image the highest-value sites at the best resolution and lighting angles, repeatedly.

buildSteps.title: Automate anomaly flagging
buildSteps.detail: Machine classifiers score each image against the baseline and pass only the strongest outliers to humans.

buildSteps.title: Characterise candidates
buildSteps.detail: Measure spectra, radar backscatter, albedo and shape remotely; a natural explanation must be ruled out, not merely absent.

buildSteps.title: Recover physical samples
buildSteps.detail: Send a rover or lander to the site, or recover fallen debris from the ocean floor after a precisely tracked fireball — the only evidence that cannot be explained away by image artefacts.

buildSteps.title: Publish and replicate
buildSteps.detail: Release raw data and methods so independent groups can confirm or refute each candidate.

prerequisites.why: lunar orbiters already image the surface at roughly half a metre per pixel, enough to see objects of metre scale.

prerequisites.tech: Routine discovery and tracking of small Solar System bodies
prerequisites.why: wide-field surveys such as the Vera C. Rubin Observatory, now beginning its decade-long survey, and asteroid-hunting space telescopes find co-orbitals and interstellar visitors.
networks of cameras and infrasound sensors can pin down where meteorites land, but coverage is uneven and most falls are never recovered.

prerequisites.tech: Automated anomaly detection at survey scale
prerequisites.why: classifiers work on terrestrial and astronomical images but have not been validated for artefact hunting, where false positives are expensive.

prerequisites.tech: Rendezvous or sample-return missions to small bodies
prerequisites.why: returning samples from an asteroid has been done, but a mission to an object on an interstellar trajectory does not yet exist.

pathway.milestone: systematic reanalysis of archival lunar imagery and sky-survey data for anomalies
pathway.unlocks: a statistical statement about what is not there, which is the honest first result.

pathway.milestone: scheduled surveys of the lunar surface, co-orbitals and Lagrange points at higher resolution and with subsurface radar
pathway.unlocks: detection of buried structures and objects too small or too dark for current imagery.

pathway.milestone: dedicated reconnaissance of any surviving candidate, plus sampling of an Earth co-orbital asteroid
pathway.unlocks: real material in a laboratory, where isotopic and manufacturing signatures can be tested.

pathway.milestone: intercept mission to an object on a confirmed interstellar trajectory
pathway.unlocks: direct examination of material manufactured outside the Solar System, if any arrives.

pathway.milestone: a standing, funded survey programme covering the whole inner Solar System
pathway.unlocks: a defensible upper limit on the number of non-human artefacts present.
